parsed.explanation: Political hostility appears substantial: government ministers have publicly framed foreign gender-recognition rules as too permissive and proposed excluding trans patients from sex-specific hospital wards. The government also curtailed recognition of certificates from numerous jurisdictions, while a statutory single-sex spaces code has prompted UN experts to warn of discrimination. These measures indicate a hostile political climate, though their practical effects and regional application remain uncertain. The record also shows continuing discrimination protections and government lawyers defending individualised prison risk assessments, so hostility is not uniformly extreme. Court rulings and police policies are not themselves direct evidence of politicians’ attitudes.
